name: Visual mark and product-name replacement
mechanism: Asset substitution plus string replacement over a declared identifier set
failure_mode: Donor mark survives in a compiled bundle, an email template, a favicon or an OG image that no source grep reaches
evidence: knowledge/00-MASTER-SYNTHESIS.md — 'Replacing a logo is trivial'
judgment_required: none
falsifier: A rendered-surface sweep finds a donor mark absent from source text

name: Token-level visual reconciliation
mechanism: Donor token map to host semantic tokens; scoped CSS boundary so donor styles do not leak
failure_mode: Flattening every donor into one generic aesthetic, destroying the donor UI quality that motivated reuse
evidence: knowledge/04-OPEN-QUESTIONS.md Q29
judgment_required: Which donor visual decisions are quality and which are merely donor identity — an aesthetic judgment no gate can make
handoff: S2-L2 owns the token contract; P04 owns only that the surgery exists and is SEMI
falsifier: A cross-donor composition passes token validation and is still judged visually incoherent by a human panel

name: Donor onboarding suppression
mechanism: Route removal or guard redirect for donor first-run wizards, sample-data seeders and welcome tours
failure_mode: Suppressed wizard also performed required initialization (default workspace, permission rows, search index), so suppression produces a silently under-initialized tenant
evidence: Teable brief success criterion 4 — 'No Teable signup/login route is reachable'
judgment_required: Distinguishing UX onboarding from initialization side effects; only readable by tracing what the wizard writes
falsifier: A tenant created with onboarding suppressed diverges in database state from one created through the donor wizard

name: Host session injection at the donor auth seam
mechanism: Two-token exchange: host backend holds the long-lived credential and mints a short-lived audience-bound single-use per-user assertion the donor guard consumes
failure_mode: Donor login route remains reachable, creating a second identity plane; or the assertion is passed as a query parameter where its plain-text identifier is attacker-manipulable
evidence: P10 pattern A — four independent commercial forms (Shopify App Bridge, Superblocks, Salesforce Canvas, monday.com) converge on two tokens; Wix is the negative control; SISOCRM Ed25519 60-120s audience-bound single-use jti was protocol-proven by an executable spike
judgment_required: Locating the smallest seam where a host session substitutes for donor auth without reimplementing donor authorization
falsifier: A donor login route is reachable after absorption, or a replayed assertion authenticates twice

name: Donor authorization model preservation
mechanism: Map host roles onto donor permission primitives without rewriting the donor authorization layer
failure_mode: Host role mapped to a broader donor role than intended, silently escalating privilege inside the donor
evidence: Composition rule C4 — the composition scope is the INTERSECTION, never the union; the natural union implementation is exactly wrong
judgment_required: Full — role semantics are product judgments and no two donors agree on what 'admin' means
falsifier: A host user performs a donor action their host role does not grant

name: Tenant key introduction and propagation
mechanism: Identify the donor tenant concept (or its absence), add a tenant key as a first-class column from the first migration, and enforce propagation at every entry point
failure_mode: Cross-tenant read or write. This is the single unrecoverable failure in the taxonomy
evidence: P09 §5 — for a TypeScript host there are effectively NO adoptable multi-tenancy frameworks; the maintained ones (archtechx/tenancy Laravel 4.4k, citusdata/django-multitenant 822) are language-locked. Tenant isolation must be budgeted as owned, tested work; no purchase removes it
judgment_required: Whether the donor's isolation is sufficient; absence of evidence is U, never a pass
falsifier: A cross-tenant result is observed under any query path

name: Proxy-enforced authorization for schema-inaccessible donors
mechanism: Host-owned proxy sets the authorization shape; client or donor subsets may only NARROW it, never widen
failure_mode: A narrowing rule that is actually a widening rule because the proxy composed scopes as a union
evidence: P09 §4 — ElectricSQL explicitly refuses to codify auth into database rules; Algolia independently proves the adjacent primitive (signed unalterable filter-bearing key, with the explicit doc line that per-tenant indices are unnecessary). The only pattern found that works WITHOUT schema access, which is the defining constraint when federating donor stores
judgment_required: Whether the proxy sees every path to the data, including donor background jobs
falsifier: A donor code path reaches data without traversing the proxy

name: Settings remount into the host hierarchy
mechanism: Re-render donor settings inside host chrome against a scoped tree with an explicit combination rule
failure_mode: Unknown at the required depth — this is the taxonomy's least-evidenced surgery
evidence: P10 HEADLINE: after 33 commercial surfaces, ZERO render a third party's settings inside host-owned chrome. Shopify, Forge and Superblocks leave the guest's settings screen wholly to the guest. Zoho One and Microsoft 365 unify at identity and admin and explicitly do NOT suppress donor chrome. This is absence of evidence after a deliberate sweep, not proof of impossibility
judgment_required: Full, and the judgment has no commercial precedent to copy
falsifier: One donor's settings surface renders inside host chrome with full functional parity and survives a donor upgrade

name: Donor-rendered settings behind a host navigation entry
mechanism: Host renders the nav entry and owns the URL; donor renders its own settings screen
failure_mode: Two settings idioms in one product, which is exactly what the commercial baseline accepts
evidence: P10 tier table — the commercial baseline; the honest v1 scope
judgment_required: none
falsifier: Client research shows the split settings surface materially damages task completion

name: Navigation contribution registration
mechanism: Donor declares nav nodes as data; host composes one tree with visibility predicates over role and entitlement
failure_mode: Duplicate silos — a donor nav rail beside the host rail, which is the default outcome of doing nothing
evidence: P10 §3 — Luigi has the declarative node structure (~45 params; children typed 'array | function' resolving at runtime; visibleForFeatureToggles with negation; userSettingsGroup tying nav to settings) but NO contribution model. Backstage decentralizes contribution but emits a React ELEMENT, not a declarative record, and is welded to @backstage/cli and webpack. Two proven halves, no whole
judgment_required: Which donor routes are product surfaces and which are internal
build_required: Actionist must build the host nav registry; neither half is adoptable
falsifier: A donor contributes nav declaratively at runtime and the host renders it gated by both role and entitlement

name: Route-space reconciliation handshake
mechanism: Host assigns the mount path; donor internal router is rebased onto it and deep links are rewritten in both directions
failure_mode: Direct URL visits break while in-app navigation works — the seam fails only on the path least likely to be tested
evidence: P10 §2 — 'the host owns the URL space, the guest owns its internal router, and the guest must reconcile them', observed WITHOUT EXCEPTION across every surveyed surface. Forge states it outright; Shopify's reported broken TitleBar links on direct URL visits are the same seam failing
judgment_required: Whether the donor router can be rebased at all, or assumes it owns root
falsifier: A deep link into an absorbed donor surface resolves correctly on a cold load

name: Cascading emptiness enforcement
mechanism: When entitlement gating hides every child, hide the parent container recursively
failure_mode: Empty chrome — a tab that opens to nothing because its only component was entitlement-stripped
evidence: P10 pattern D — Salesforce is the only surface that specifies it; Frontegg supplies the two-gate rule (role permission AND feature entitlement, at different scopes so neither folds into the other)
judgment_required: none
falsifier: An entitlement-stripped donor leaves a reachable empty container

name: Migration authority assignment
mechanism: Name exactly one migration owner per resource and record it in the BindingPlan
failure_mode: Two migration owners over one table. Documenso renames a column, Papermark does not know, it breaks at 2am mid-deal
evidence: SISOCRM OWNERSHIP-AND-DATA-LAYER-DECISIONS — 'One shared schema, donors rewritten to it' was explicitly rejected because it couples independently-versioned projects at their most brittle layer; A11 'one owner per table and migration, never two'
judgment_required: Full — this is a product-architecture decision, not a mechanical one
falsifier: Two migration histories are observed touching one table

name: Schema-per-donor placement in one database server
mechanism: Each donor keeps its own migration history in its own schema on one shared Postgres server
failure_mode: Cross-schema joins are gone; the answer that spans two donors must be assembled elsewhere
evidence: SISOCRM — chosen over separate DB servers (operationally silly on one VPS) and over one shared schema (couples five projects). Honest stated cost: 'which buyers signed an NDA AND viewed the CIM' cannot be one query. The trade is sharing the OPERATIONAL burden without sharing the COUPLING
judgment_required: Whether the donor tolerates a non-default schema and search path at all
falsifier: A donor requires a dedicated database or hardcodes its schema name

name: Event-fed read model for cross-owner views
mechanism: Consume donor events into host-owned tables; query the host tables for any view spanning owners
failure_mode: Silent dual write — the read model is mutated directly and diverges from its source of truth
evidence: A12; SISOCRM Svix and the event envelope exist precisely to pay this cost
judgment_required: Whether eventual consistency is acceptable for this specific product view, or synchronous consistency is genuinely required
falsifier: A read model is written by anything other than its event consumer

name: Pre-absorption migration state capture
mechanism: Snapshot the donor migration head and the database dump before any absorption migration runs
failure_mode: No restore point, so the absorption is irreversible in practice regardless of what the rollback plan claims
evidence: SISOCRM donor-fork required proof includes 'backup-before-migration'; P14 — data rollback is a separate object with its own horizon
judgment_required: none
falsifier: A rollback drill cannot restore pre-absorption state

name: Donor event surface normalization
mechanism: Wrap heterogeneous donor webhooks and internal events in one host envelope with a stable capability identifier
failure_mode: Events attributed to the application rather than the capability, making per-capability failure attribution impossible later
evidence: P14 minimum instrumentation contract item 1 — capability identity must be deliberately PLURAL where the app is one thing but the capabilities are many
judgment_required: Which donor internal events are contractual and which are incidental
falsifier: An event cannot be attributed to a single capability identifier

name: Tenant connection store ownership
mechanism: Host owns the tenant-scoped connection table; donor or catalogue supplies only provider definitions and OAuth mechanics
failure_mode: Cross-tenant credential exposure
evidence: A26 REJECTED by demonstration, not inference: OpenConnector's connections table is keyed (service, connection_name) with NO tenant column; oauth_client_configs is keyed on service alone (one OAuth app per service globally); the key salt is a hardcoded constant; the secret codec silently returns PLAINTEXT when the env key is unset; and two named tenants' connections were returned together under one admin token during the 27 Aug spike
judgment_required: none — the store is unfit as inherited
falsifier: Two tenants' credentials are retrievable under one token

name: Catalogue and OAuth mechanics adoption without storage
mechanism: Reuse generated provider definitions and OAuth authorization-URL construction; discard the connection persistence layer
failure_mode: Inheriting the storage layer along with the catalogue because they ship together
evidence: A27 observed at spike level: 1,445 providers and 15,156 actions generated from repository source with no network; a fake token rejected by live credential verification before persistence; a correctly parameterized OAuth URL with access_type=offline and encrypted state
judgment_required: Where the catalogue ends and the storage begins in the donor's own code
falsifier: The catalogue cannot be generated without instantiating the connection store

name: Idempotency layer placement
mechanism: Place the host idempotency layer INSIDE the rate limiter and auth check, not outside
failure_mode: A request rate-limited with a 429 produces a different result under the same key, so the key does not make the request safe to replay
evidence: P11 — Stripe's rate limiters run BEFORE its idempotency layer; the same holds for a 401 with a missing key and most 400s. The safety window opens only once the request reaches the idempotency layer. Actionist reproduces this hazard at its own boundary if it copies the ordering. Separately: OSS supply for idempotency is effectively absent (most-starred middleware found: 14 stars) and no surveyed embedded-iPaaS or agent-action vendor documented a write idempotency contract
judgment_required: Whether to cache failure responses (stable replay answer, but pins a transient error) or not (a genuine retry can succeed) — a deliberate Actionist decision, not an inherited default
falsifier: Two identical requests under one key produce different side effects

name: Dry-run preview for external effects
mechanism: Resolve and return the exact arguments with empty results and no side effect; on by default and not tenant-disableable
failure_mode: An agent takes an irreversible external action whose arguments nobody inspected
evidence: P11 best single primitive: Zapier's preview_only, forceable by the action author so the tenant cannot disable it. Caveat: Zapier AI Actions is documented as no longer developed or supported — a pattern to study, not a dependency
judgment_required: none
falsifier: An external-effecting port executes without an available dry run

name: Donor token extraction and semantic mapping
mechanism: Enumerate donor design tokens, map to host semantic tokens, resolve through ONE resolver context
failure_mode: Hardcoded values that no token map reaches, so the donor stays visually foreign under theming
evidence: Composition rule C3; siso-ui-base gates dna-grep and principles-grep with the explicit precedence 'where they disagree THE DNA WINS'
judgment_required: Which donor values are semantic and which are incidental
falsifier: A themed donor surface still renders donor-branded colours

name: Runtime profile selection
mechanism: Choose package, microfrontend, iframe, sidecar, service, worker or cron for this capability in this application
failure_mode: Choosing an embedded profile for something engine-shaped, converting a dependency-update problem into a permanent fork
evidence: repo-to-block §3.3 — an S3 decision made for convenience when S1 was available is a review failure; Q39 lists the seven candidate profiles as unresolved
judgment_required: Full — this is the shape decision and it is not revisable without restarting
falsifier: A capability's runtime profile is changed without re-qualification

name: Background job and scheduler reconciliation
mechanism: Decide which donor jobs, queues and cron entries remain donor-operated and which the host schedules
failure_mode: A suppressed donor job silently stops maintaining state the donor UI assumes is fresh
evidence: Teable brief recon question 4 — 'What background jobs / queues / cron does it run, and what do they need?'
judgment_required: Which jobs are load-bearing for correctness versus convenience
falsifier: A donor surface displays stale data after absorption because its refresh job was dropped

name: Upstream drift detection and response
mechanism: Digest comparison against current upstream (DET) followed by a named human adopt/hold/fork/retire decision (HUM)
failure_mode: Drift accumulates until the merge is no longer attempted, and the pinned fork silently becomes vendored-no-upstream
evidence: repo-to-block §3.10; SISOCRM test — 'Would upstream ever ship something here that we would actually want?' Yes: stay downstream, their patches are a gift. No: take the code, the merge is fiction
judgment_required: The response is irreducibly human; only the detection is mechanical
falsifier: An upstream security fix is not applied within the declared window

name: Transplant re-extraction burden
mechanism: Re-extract and re-adapt an upstream fix into an already-adapted slice, resolving conflicts with local adaptation
failure_mode: The worst recurring cost in the taxonomy, and the reason coordinate-only shapes are preferred wherever available
evidence: repo-to-block §3.10 — 'S3 slices carry the worst case'
judgment_required: Whether the fix is worth the re-extraction at all
falsifier: Re-extraction cost exceeds rewriting the slice

name: Multi-object rollback plan construction
mechanism: Enumerate every recoverable object with its restore procedure and horizon; compute the composition horizon as the minimum
failure_mode: A boolean rollback claim that reverts code and leaves configuration, secrets, schema, data and donor revision untouched
evidence: P14 §3 derived twice independently — Vercel reverts traffic in ~1s but not env vars or configuration; Fly does not revert fly.toml, secrets or migrations; SISOCRM: 'Data rollback is separate: restore the pre-migration database dump', plus a third object no vendor surfaced (a standing alternate UI route)
judgment_required: Which objects are genuinely independent and what each horizon actually is
falsifier: A rollback drill restores code and leaves any other object at the new version

name: Artifact retention under host ownership
mechanism: Pin by content digest AND retain the artifact in Actionist-owned storage for at least the declared horizon
failure_mode: Rollback re-pulls by tag and obtains a different image, or the image was pruned
evidence: P14 §5 — Render re-pulls by tag on rollback; Fly warns images not recently deployed may be pruned. A pinned reference to an artifact a third party may garbage-collect is not a recovery path
judgment_required: none
falsifier: A rollback obtains an artifact whose digest differs from the released one
